- Remove the GitHub activity component from dashboard 
 - Grey out and lock the next modules when the user has not finished the current one in the Learn index route where the modules are listed. Also the "Continue" CTA should only be shown on the current module. Completed modules should be moved to the bottom of the page, but not disabled
- Improve the fullscreen feature to fully cover the viewport as expected. This is useful for interactive previews of the user's sketch. 
- When you click on an achievement badge on the dashboard show a popup that shows the badge's full details including the date it was attained. Allow the user to swipe left/right to see the next/prev achievements whilst the popup is active
- Remove the Debugging settings option and all associated code
- During build, always bundle the latest p5.js version
- In the exercise view's reference popup (the one showed when we long press the Run button), show the selected symbol's content in that popup instead of navigating away. This avoids disruption and keeps the user in the current exercise view as they would expect. 
- Syntax highlight the example code in the Reference route instead of rendering it as plain text. Also ensure that it respects themeing
I'll research the codebase to understand each area before forming a plan. Let me explore inparallel.

'⛶' : '✕'; if (!isExpanded) { setTimeout(function() { smoothScrollTo(sketch, 300); }, 350); } } }); } ``` **Why it does not cover the full viewport:** The handler only toggles the `.expanded` CSS class, which resizes the `#user-sketch` box from `180px` → `400px` tall (and never modifies width). There is no `requestFullscreen` anywhere in `exerciseHtml.ts` (confirmed by grep — only `smoothScrollTo` matches). The sketch remains inline within the scrollable WebView document, constrained to a `400px`-tall box and the WebView's own width. To make it cover the full viewport, the handler would need either `sketch.requestFullscreen()` or a fixed-position overlay style (`position:fixed; top:0; left:0; width:100vw; height:100vh; z-index:9999`). `smoothScrollTo` helper is defined at `:802`. --- ## 2. setSearchVisible(true); Haptics.impactAsync(Haptics.ImpactFeedbackStyle.Light).catch(() => {}); }, 600); }, []); const handleRunPressOut = useCallback(() => { if (longPressTimerRef.current) { clearTimeout(longPressTimerRef.current); }} /> ``` ### The popup component **`src/components/SearchOverlay.tsx`** (190 lines) — a `Modal` with a Fuse.js fuzzy search over `P5_SYMBOLS`. Key behavior: - `:21-33` — Fuse index built once over `P5_SYMBOLS` (`keys: name/description/module`, `threshold: 0.4`). - `:35-38` — results: empty query shows first 20 symbols; otherwise `fuse.search`. - `:46-58` — comment explains the imperative focus is specifically needed for "the Run-button long-press path from [id].tsx", because the Modal is always mounted and `autoFocus` only fires once; it focuses the input after a 60 ms delay so the keyboard reliably opens. - `:53-58`: ```tsx useEffect(() => { if (!visible) return; setQuery(""); const t = setTimeout(() => inputRef.current?.focus(), 60); return () => clearTimeout(t); }, [visible]); ``` - `:61-119` — the `Modal` UI (magnify search bar, FlatList of `name()` + module rows; selecting a row calls `onSelectSymbol(sym.name)`). 11: 
12: export const ACHIEVEMENTS: Achievement[] = [
13:   {
14:     id: "first-strokes",
15:     title: "First Strokes",
16:     subtitle: "Complete your first exercise",
17:     icon: "brush-variant",
18:     rule: "first completion event",

24:     icon: "calendar-check",
25:     rule: "3 exercises on the same calendar day",
26:   },
27:   {
28:     id: "quickdraw",
29:     title: "Quickdraw",
30:     subtitle: "Complete an exercise in under 30 seconds",
31:     icon: "timer-sand",
32:     rule: "durationMs < 30000",
33:   },
34:   {
35:     id: "on-a-roll",
36:     title: "On a Roll",
37:     subtitle: "Complete 3 exercises within 10 minutes",
38:     icon: "lightning-bolt",
39:     rule: "3 events within a 10-minute window",
40:   },
41:   {
42:     id: "weekender",
43:     title: "Weekender",
44:     subtitle: "Reach a 7-day streak",
45:     icon: "trophy",
46:     rule: "streak_count >= 7",
47:   },
48: ];
49: 
50: interface CompletionEvent {
51:   ts: number;
52:   exerciseId: string;
53:   durationMs?: number;
54: }
55: 
56: const UNLOCKED_KEY = "achievements_unlocked";
57: const EVENTS_KEY = "completion_events";
58: 
59: function dateKey(ts: number): string {
60:   return new Date(ts).toISOString().split("T")[0];
61: }
62: 
63: /**
64:  * Record a completion event and return the list of achievement IDs that
65:  * became newly unlocked as a result (idempotent on exerciseId per day —
66:  * re-running the same exercise on the same day does not double-count).
67:  */
68: export async function recordCompletion(
69:   exerciseId: string,
70:   durationMs?: number
71: ): Promise<string[]> {
72:   const eventsRaw = await AsyncStorage.getItem(EVENTS_KEY);
73:   const events: CompletionEvent[] = eventsRaw ? JSON.parse(eventsRaw) : [];
74: 
75:   // De-duplicate by exerciseId within today's date bucket.
76:   const today = dateKey(Date.now());
77:   const alreadyToday = events.some(
78:     (e) => e.exerciseId === exerciseId && dateKey(e.ts) === today
79:   );
80:   if (!alreadyToday) {
81:     events.push({ ts: Date.now(), exerciseId, durationMs });
82:     await AsyncStorage.setItem(EVENTS_KEY, JSON.stringify(events));
83:   }
84: 
85:   const unlockedRaw = await AsyncStorage.getItem(UNLOCKED_KEY);
86:   const unlocked: string[] = unlockedRaw ? JSON.parse(unlockedRaw) : [];
87:   const newlyUnlocked: string[] = [];
88: 
89:   function grant(id: string, predicate: () => boolean) {
90:     if (!unlocked.includes(id) && !newlyUnlocked.includes(id) && predicate()) {
91:       newlyUnlocked.push(id);
92:       unlocked.push(id);
93:     }
94:   }
95: 
96:   const todays = events.filter((e) => dateKey(e.ts) === today);
97: 
98:   grant("first-strokes", () => events.length >= 1);
99:   grant("daily-3", () => todays.length >= 3);
100:   grant("quickdraw", () => events.some((e) => (e.durationMs ?? Infinity) < 30000));
101: 
102:   // On a Roll: 3 events within any 10-minute window.
103:   grant("on-a-roll", () => {
104:     if (events.length < 3) return false;
105:     const sorted = [...events].sort((a, b) => a.ts - b.ts);
106:     for (let i = 2; i < sorted.length; i++) {
107:       if (sorted[i].ts - sorted[i - 2].ts <= 10 * 60 * 1000) return true;
108:     }
109:     return false;
110:   });
111: 
112:   // Weekender: streak >= 7. Read live so the badge can unlock the moment
113:   // the streak crosses the threshold, independent of completion timing.
114:   const streakCountStr = await AsyncStorage.getItem("streak_count");
115:   const streakCount = streakCountStr ? parseInt(streakCountStr, 10) : 0;
116:   grant("weekender", () => streakCount >= 7);
117: 
118:   if (newlyUnlocked.length > 0) {
119:     await AsyncStorage.setItem(UNLOCKED_KEY, JSON.stringify(unlocked));
120:   }
121: 
122:   return newlyUnlocked;
123: }
124: 
125: export async function getUnlockedAchievements(): Promise<string[]> {
126:   const raw = await AsyncStorage.getItem(UNLOCKED_KEY);
127:   return raw ? JSON.parse(raw) : [];
128: }
129: 
130: export function useAchievements() {
131:   const [unlocked, setUnlocked] = useState<string[]>([]);
132: 
133:   const refresh = useCallback(async () => {
134:     setUnlocked(await getUnlockedAchievements());
135:   }, []);
136: 
137:   useEffect(() => {
138:     refresh();
139:   }, [refresh]);
140: 
141:   return { unlocked, refresh };
142: }

I have all the information needed. Here is the comprehensive implementation plan.

## Implementation Plan

### Task 1: Remove GitHub activity component from dashboard
**Files:** `src/app/dashboard.tsx`, `src/components/ActivityHeatmap.tsx`, `src/hooks/useActivityLog.ts`

- In `dashboard.tsx`: remove the `ActivityHeatmap` import (L17), `useActivityLog` import (L16), the `useActivityLog()` hook call (L46), `refreshActivity()` calls in `useFocusEffect` (L73) and `useEffect` (L84), and the `<ActivityHeatmap activity={activity} />` render at L545.
- Delete `src/components/ActivityHeatmap.tsx` entirely.
- Delete `src/hooks/useActivityLog.ts` entirely (only consumer was the dashboard). Note: this means `completion_events` AsyncStorage reads in `useActivityLog` go away — but `useAchievements.ts` has its own independent `completion_events` read, so achievements still work.
- Verify no other imports of `ActivityHeatmap` or `useActivityLog` exist (grep confirmed only dashboard uses them).

### Task 2: Lock + grey-out upcoming modules in Learn index; "Continue" only on current module; completed modules to bottom (not disabled)
**Files:** `src/app/learn/index.tsx`, `src/components/ExerciseCard.tsx`

Currently `learn/index.tsx` lists all courses flat with a "Continue" button on every card. The user wants this to behave like per-course gating: only the *current* (first-incomplete) module shows "Continue"; later modules are greyed out & locked; completed modules move to bottom (still tappable, not disabled).

- In `learn/index.tsx`:
  - Load `completedLessons` and `completedCourses` from AsyncStorage and track in state (currently only `courses` is loaded).
  - Compute, for each course: `isCompleted` (all exercises in the course are in `completedLessons`, OR the course slug is in `completedCourses`), and `isCurrent` (the first course in order that is not completed). Determine "current" as the first course whose progress < 100%.
  - Sort render order: incomplete courses in original order first (with the current one first naturally), then completed courses at the bottom.
  - For each card pass `locked` = not current AND not completed (i.e. an upcoming module the user hasn't reached). Pass `onContinue` only when `isCurrent`.
  - Greyed appearance is handled by `ExerciseCard`'s existing `opacity: locked ? 0.5 : 1` and lock icon (already present).
- `ExerciseCard.tsx` already supports `locked` and optional `onContinue`; no changes needed beyond wiring. The `disabled`-style tap-block isn't in the card — for locked courses we just don't pass `onContinue` and optionally wrap in `Pressable disabled`. Since the card has no `onPress` of its own currently (it just shows a Button), we should wrap locked cards so the whole card is non-interactive or grey-out only. Simplest: keep card as-is; locked cards have no Continue button and show the lock icon. Tapping isn't possible anyway since there's no onPress on the card body.
- "Continue" CTA only on current module: handled by conditionally passing `onContinue`.

### Task 3: Improve fullscreen to fully cover viewport
**File:** `src/utils/editor/exerciseHtml.ts`

- Update the `.sketch-box.expanded` CSS (L172-186) to use fixed positioning covering the viewport:
  ```
  position: fixed; top: 0; left: 0; width: 100vw; height: 100vh; z-index: 9999; border-radius: 0;
  ```
- Add an exit affordance: when expanded, the maximize icon toggles to ✕ (already does, L1357). Also add a close button overlay or allow tapping the icon again. The existing handler already toggles, so this works. Optionally add `background:#000` so the fullscreen canvas is against black.
- Consider that the WebView itself constrains the viewport: in RN the WebView fills a fixed-height container. `100vh` inside the WebView refers to the WebView's CSS viewport, which equals the WebView's pixel height. If the WebView is only 400px tall, `100vh` = 400px, not the screen. To truly cover the device viewport, the toggle should also message the RN host to expand the WebView container to fill the screen — that's a bigger change. **Recommendation:** Use the document Fullscreen API inside the WebView: `sketchBox.requestFullscreen()` (with `webkitRequestFullscreen` fallback) on expand, and `document.exitFullscreen()` on collapse. The WebView's `<canvas>` then covers the whole OS viewport. Add fullscreenchange listener to keep the icon in sync. This is the cleanest "fully cover the viewport" solution without RN-side layout changes.
- Since `smoothScrollTo` becomes irrelevant in fullscreen, keep it for non-fullscreen scroll but it's fine.

### Task 4: Achievement badge popup with date + swipe left/right
**Files:** `src/app/dashboard.tsx`, new `src/components/AchievementBadgeModal.tsx`, `src/hooks/useAchievements.ts`

- Achievements are unlocked and stored in `achievements_unlocked` as `string[]`. There's NO date currently stored. To show the date attained, we need to record it. Modify `recordCompletion` in `useAchievements.ts` to store `achievements_unlocked` as a map/`Record<string, string>` (id → ISO timestamp) OR add a parallel `achievements_unlocked_at` key. To preserve backward compat with existing arrays, use a NEW key `achievements_unlocked_at` (id → ISO date) written alongside `achievements_unlocked`. `useAchievements` exposes `unlockedAt: Record<string,string>` too.
- New `AchievementBadgeModal.tsx`: a `Modal` showing the selected badge's full details — icon, title, subtitle, rule, and "Earned <formatted date>" (or "Locked" if somehow selected but not unlocked). Implements horizontal swipe via `react-native-gesture-handler`'s `GestureDetector` with a pan gesture (the lib is already a dep, v2.30.0) OR a simpler `FlatList` with `horizontal` + `pagingEnabled` to render the user's unlocked badges and let them swipe between them. `pagingEnabled` FlatList is simplest and robust. Tapping a badge on the dashboard opens the modal at the tapped badge's index.
- In `dashboard.tsx`: wrap each `achievementCircle` in a `Pressable` that sets `badgeModalIndex` and `badgeModalVisible`. Render `<AchievementBadgeModal visible indices unlocked achievements unlockedAt ... />`.
- Format date with `toLocaleDateString()`.

### Task 5: Remove Debugging settings option + all associated code
**Files:** `src/app/settings/index.tsx`, `src/app/settings/error-logs.tsx`, `src/app/learn/[course]/[id].tsx`

- In `settings/index.tsx`: remove the entire Debugging section (L622-748): SectionHeader, devMode toggle, and the `devMode && (...)` block (Error Logs button, Show Toast, Show Streak, Complete All, Reset All, Set Streak). Remove `devMode` state (L107), its load (L141), `toggleDevMode` (L234-237), `handleCompleteAllExercises` (L254-265), `handleResetAllProgress` (L267-272), `handleSetStreak` (L274-282), `debugToastVisible`/`debugStreakToastVisible`/`debugStreakCount` state (L111-113), the SETTINGS_KEYS.devMode entry (L37), and the `<Toast>`/`<StreakToast>` debug modal renders (L791-800).
- Delete `src/app/settings/error-logs.tsx` entirely.
- In `src/app/learn/[course]/[id].tsx`: remove the two `error_log` AsyncStorage writers — at L378-388 (load failure) and L466-479 (sketchError runtime). Replace with just the dispatch calls. Remove the `error_log`-related code but keep the error display to the user via existing dispatch/state.
- Double check no other references to `error_log` or `/settings/error-logs` route remain.

### Task 6: During build, always bundle the latest p5.js version
**Files:** new `scripts/bundle-p5.mjs`, `src/utils/p5Source.ts` (generated), `scripts/generate-reference.mjs`, `package.json`, `AGENTS.md`

- New `scripts/bundle-p5.mjs`: queries `https://registry.npmjs.org/p5/latest` (or `p5` packument `dist-tags.latest`), fetches the tarball's `lib/p5.min.js`, and **rewrites `src/utils/p5Source.ts`** preserving the exact existing hand-authored structure: the `const _p = [ ... ]; export const p5Source = _p.join("")` shape with the minified source as a single string-literal element (escaping backticks/`${}`/backslashes as needed), and updates the header comment with the resolved version + jsDelivr URL. Also writes the resolved version to a shared file (e.g. `src/data/p5-version.json` or just re-reads the package.json-stored version) so `generate-reference.mjs` can stamp `p5Version` from it instead of hardcoded `"2.3.0"`.
  - Respect the existing hardcode convention: keep it as a vendored string literal (offline-safe at runtime), just regenerated each build. The user explicitly said "make sure it respects how the current p5.js library is hardcoded." So we keep the `_p` array + `p5Source` export format; the script regenerates the file.
- Update `scripts/generate-reference.mjs` L92: read the version from the freshly written `p5Source.ts` header comment or from a sidecar `p5-version.json`. Simplest: `bundle-p5.mjs` writes the version to `src/utils/p5-source.version.txt` and `generate-reference.mjs` reads it (falling back to "2.3.0" if missing). Or, to keep concerns clean, have `bundle-p5.mjs` export the version via the same generated .ts file as an additional `export const p5Version = "X.Y.Z"`. ## Course modules (YAML → TS build artifacts)

- **Source of truth: `src/data/courses/*.yaml`** — edit YAML, never the `.ts` files.
- `scripts/build-courses.mjs` reads every `.yaml` in `src/data/courses/` and emits a matching `.ts` next to it (`<slug>Course` export).

## p5.js bundling (always latest)

- `scripts/bundle-p5.mjs` queries the npm registry for the latest `p5` release, downloads `lib/p5.min.js`, and regenerates `src/utils/p5Source.ts` (the vendored minified source as `const _p = [...]; export const p5Source = _p.join("")`) plus `src/utils/p5Version.ts` (`export const p5Version = "X.Y.Z"`).
- `bundle-p5` runs first in `postinstall` (before `gen-reference`) and first in `npm start`, so the app always bundles the newest p5.js. `scripts/generate-reference.mjs` reads the version stamp from `src/utils/p5Version.ts` instead of hardcoding it.
- **`src/utils/p5Source.ts` and `src/utils/p5Version.ts` are gitignored build artifacts** — never commit them. A fresh clone regenerates them on `npm install`.
